chunks: And he, peace be upon him, said:
There is no usury between a man and his child, and there is no usury between a master and his servant.

key_terms.الرَّجُلِ: the man; here, the father or male parent in the stated relationship
key_terms.السَّيِّدِ: the master; the owner in relation to a servant or slave
key_terms.رِبًا: usury; unlawfully increased excess in a financial transaction
key_terms.عَبْدِهِ: his servant; the owned bondman in this legal context
key_terms.لَيْسَ: is not; negates the applicability of the ruling
key_terms.وَلَدِهِ: his child; the offspring in relation to the parent

ai.seo_question: Is riba applicable between a man and his child or between a master and his servant in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning riba, declaring that it does not apply between a man and his child, nor between a master and his servant. It belongs to the jurisprudential discussion of financial dealings and defines exceptions within specific dependent relationships.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: "There is no usury between a man and his child, and there is no usury between a master and his servant."
